name: Strawberries and Cream Tree
text: Your train passes near the Strawberries and Cream Tree in Backwell, on the train's {side}, a cherry tree with white blossom on one side and pink on the other: a wild cherry grafted with a Japanese one. Children in Backwell gave it its name.

name: St Mary's Church, Yatton
text: Your train passes near St Mary's Church in Yatton, on the train's {side}, built around 1400. It is often called the Cathedral of the Moors, as it is so large for the village.

name: The Helicopter Museum
text: Your train passes near the Helicopter Museum, on the train's {side}, with more than 80 helicopters and autogyros from around the world. It began as the private collection of the aviation writer Elfan ap Rees and opened to the public in 1978.

name: Castle Street, Bridgwater
text: Your train passes near Castle Street in Bridgwater, on the train's {side}, built in the 1720s for the Duke of Chandos on the site of Bridgwater Castle. Many of its houses are listed Grade I.

name: Tropicana (Dismaland)
text: Your train passes near the Tropicana, a disused lido in Weston-super-Mare, on the train's {side}, where Banksy secretly built Dismaland, his "bemusement park", in 2015. It was open for 36 days and had 150,000 visitors.

name: Grand Pier, Weston-super-Mare
text: Your train passes near Weston-super-Mare's Grand Pier, on the train's {side}, opened in 1904. Its pavilion has burned down twice, in 1930 and in 2008.

name: Worle Town station (site)
text: Your train passes near the site of Worle Town station, on the train's {side}, on the Weston, Clevedon and Portishead Railway. It opened in 1897 and closed in May 1940; with no gates at its level crossing, it saw several accidents.

name: Stoke Gifford depot
text: Your train passes Stoke Gifford depot, on the train's {side}, opened in 2016 on a triangle of land between three railway lines. It looks after Great Western Railway's Class 800 trains.

name: Gipsy Patch Lane Bridge
text: Your train crosses Gipsy Patch Lane on a bridge built in 2020. It replaced a narrow dark-brick arch, so that the road could have a bus lane each way.

name: The Wave
text: Your train passes near The Wave, on the train's {side}, an artificial lake for surfing that opened in 2019, with wave machines from the Spanish company Wavegarden.

name: Severn Tunnel
text: Your train runs through the Severn Tunnel under the estuary of the River Severn, opened in 1886. It is 7,008 metres long, and until 1987 it was the longest underwater tunnel in the world.

name: Huckford Viaduct
text: Your train crosses the Huckford Viaduct, built by the Great Western Railway in 1902 about 100 feet above the River Frome, which runs through one of its arches.

name: Holy Trinity Church, Wickwar
text: Your train passes near Holy Trinity, Wickwar's parish church, on the train's {side}. It stands on a small hill, reached by a raised path called the Stank, meaning "dam": there were fish ponds here until the 1800s.

name: Frocester Court barn
text: Your train passes near the barn at Frocester Court, on the train's {side}, a late 13th-century estate barn listed Grade I. The remains of a Roman villa have been found in the grounds.

name: Stonehouse Court
text: Your train passes near Stonehouse Court, on the train's {side}, a manor house of 1601 that is now a hotel. An earlier owner of the manor, John Maltravers, was found guilty of a part in the murder of Edward II in 1327.

name: Dean Close School
text: Your train passes near Dean Close School, on the train's {side}, opened in 1886. Its grounds, some 50 acres, are the largest single private area of land in Cheltenham.

name: Siege of Gloucester
text: Your train passes near the centre of Gloucester, on the train's {side}, which held out against Charles I's army for nearly four weeks in 1643, until a Parliamentarian army under the Earl of Essex arrived and the siege was lifted.

name: Stanley Mills
text: Your train passes near Stanley Mills, on the train's {side}, a woollen mill built in 1813 to be fireproof, with cast-iron columns holding up brick vaults. Five waterwheels on the River Frome once drove it, and its main building is listed Grade I.

name: Sapperton Canal Tunnel
text: Your train passes near one end of the Sapperton Canal Tunnel, on the train's {side}. When it opened in 1789 it was the longest tunnel of any kind in England, and it kept the title until 1811. Boats were legged through it until 1911.

name: Swindon Mechanics' Institute
text: Your train passes near the Mechanics' Institute in Swindon, on the train's {side}, founded in 1843 to give evening classes and a library to the Great Western Railway's workers. Its building of 1854 and 1855 has stood empty since the works closed in 1986.

name: St Barnabas Church, Oxford
text: Your train passes near St Barnabas Church in Jericho, Oxford, on the train's {side}, built like an Italian basilica with a bell tower. It appears in Thomas Hardy's Jude the Obscure, and John Betjeman wrote a poem about it.

name: Blenheim Palace
text: Your train passes near the park of Blenheim Palace, on the train's {side}, built between 1705 and 1722 and now a World Heritage Site. Winston Churchill was born there.

name: North Leigh Roman Villa
text: Your train passes near North Leigh Roman Villa, on the train's {side}, which grew from the late first century into a very large, luxurious house with 19 mosaic floors. It is in the care of English Heritage.

name: Cornbury Park
text: Your train runs along the edge of Cornbury Park, on the train's {side}, once a royal hunting estate: Domesday Book calls it a "demesne forest of the king". It still holds a remnant of the Wychwood Forest.

name: Ascot d'Oilly Castle
text: Your train passes near the mound of Ascot d'Oilly Castle, on the train's {side}, named after Roger d'Oilly, who was given the land by William the Conqueror. His brother built Oxford Castle.

name: Ascott Earl Castle
text: Your train passes near the mound of Ascott Earl Castle, on the train's {side}, a motte-and-bailey castle built on Iron Age earthworks. A second castle, Ascot d'Oilly, stands at the other end of the village.

name: Bruern Abbey
text: Your train passes near Bruern Abbey, on the train's {side}, where Nicholas Basset founded a Cistercian abbey in 1147. The country house there now was built in 1720.

name: Adlestrop (former station)
text: Your train passes the site of Adlestrop station, closed in 1966. On June 24th 1914 the poet Edward Thomas's express made a stop here, and he wrote the poem "Adlestrop" about it; a station sign and a bench are now in the village bus shelter.

name: Roman town at Dorn
text: Your train runs past the site of a small Roman town at Dorn, the largest of five defended towns on the Fosse Way between Cirencester and Lincoln. Here the line reaches its highest point between Oxford and Worcester.

name: Battle of Evesham
text: Your train passes the battlefield of Evesham, on the train's {side}, where on August 4th 1265 the future Edward I defeated Simon de Montfort, who was killed in the fighting.

name: Evesham Abbey bell tower
text: Your train passes near the bell tower of Evesham Abbey, on the train's {side}, built in the 1500s. Almost all of the abbey was pulled down at the Dissolution, but the tower still stands.

name: Mucknell Abbey
text: Your train passes near Mucknell Abbey, on the train's {side}, an Anglican Benedictine monastery of monks and nuns on what was a farm. The community moved here from Burford Priory.

name: The Commandery
text: Your train passes near the Commandery in Worcester, on the train's {side}, the Royalist army's headquarters at the Battle of Worcester on September 3rd 1651. It is listed Grade I and open to visitors.

name: Worcester Cathedral
text: Your train passes near Worcester Cathedral, on the train's {side}, founded in 680. King John, who died in 1216, is buried there.

name: Worcester Racecourse
text: Your train passes near Worcester Racecourse, known locally as Pitchcroft, on the train's {side}, beside the River Severn. Horses have raced there since at least 1718.

name: Great Malvern Priory
text: Your train passes near Great Malvern Priory, on the train's {side}, a Benedictine monastery from about 1075 and now the parish church. It has the largest display of 15th-century stained glass in England.

name: Colwall Tunnel
text: Your train runs through the Colwall Tunnel under the Malvern Hills. The first tunnel here opened in 1861; it was replaced on August 2nd 1926 by the wider one in use today.

name: Ledbury Tunnel
text: Your train runs through Ledbury Tunnel, bored through the limestone of Dog Hill and opened in 1861. It has never been widened, and carries a single track for its whole length of 1,323 yards.

name: Hereford Cathedral
text: Your train passes near Hereford Cathedral, on the train's {side}, home of the Mappa Mundi, a map of the world made around 1300, and of the largest library of chained books in the world.

name: Bredon Barn
text: Your train passes near Bredon Barn, on the train's {side}, a 14th-century barn built for the Bishops of Worcester. The National Trust has had it since 1951; it was badly damaged by fire in 1979 and restored by 1983.
